prompt:
You are screening bibliographic records for inclusion in the DESTINY repository, a database of the global literature at the intersection of climate change and health, including climate mitigation and adaptation.

Classify each record as INCLUDE or EXCLUDE, based only on the title, abstract, and metadata provided.

THIS IS THE HIGH-RECALL SCREEN. The goal is to miss as few relevant records as possible; a later stage will remove false positives. Do not require climate change, health, mitigation, or adaptation to be the primary topic, or to be studied in depth -- a substantive or clearly-signalled presence is enough. When the criteria are plausibly met, or you are genuinely uncertain, choose INCLUDE.

CORE DECISION RULE
INCLUDE when BOTH are present:
1. A CLIMATE-RELATED element, AND
2. A HEALTH, MITIGATION, or ADAPTATION element.
When in doubt about either, INCLUDE.

--------------------------------------------------
1. CLIMATE-RELATED element
--------------------------------------------------
Present when the record mentions or engages any of:
- Climate change or climate variability -- INCLUDING thematic, policy, or framework-level engagement (e.g. the Paris / UNFCCC Climate Change Agreements, and cross-framework synergies that involve climate). A theme-level engagement with climate change counts; it need not be the study of a specific climate variable.
- Weather or climate variables (temperature, precipitation, humidity, wind, drought, heat, cold, and other weather/climate conditions).
- Climate-related extreme events (heatwaves, cold spells, floods, droughts, storms, cyclones/hurricanes/typhoons, storm surges, wildfires, landslides, sea-level rise). Their attribution to climate change need not be stated.
- Fossil fuels or fossil-fuel use (coal, oil, natural gas, petroleum, diesel, petrol, LNG/CNG, etc.).
- Greenhouse gases or other climate-forcing agents (CO2, methane, nitrous oxide, F-gases; tropospheric ozone and ozone-depleting substances).
- Aerosols / particulate matter (PM2.5, PM10, black carbon, organic carbon, sulfate/nitrate aerosols, smoke, haze, air pollutants). A mention of particulate matter or air pollutants is SUFFICIENT on its own for this criterion -- these are recognised climate-forcing/climate-relevant agents.

NARROW EXCEPTIONS (these do NOT by themselves establish the climate element -- everywhere else, read it inclusively):
- A fossil fuel or climate-forcing agent that appears ONLY for a non-climate reason: as a recreational drug (e.g. nitrous-oxide abuse), as an industrial-accident or safety hazard (e.g. a pipeline explosion), or as the subject of pollution cleanup unrelated to emissions or climate.
- Routine weather as the mere operating environment of a device or activity (e.g. a sensor or vehicle system tested under rain or snow). An actual climate-related hazard (flood, storm, drought, heatwave, etc.) still qualifies.

--------------------------------------------------
2. HEALTH, MITIGATION, or ADAPTATION element
--------------------------------------------------
Present when ANY ONE of the following applies:

(a) HEALTH -- the record touches human health or health systems, EITHER
   - directly (disease, illness, symptoms, morbidity, mortality, injury, exposure, health risk, occupational health, public health, healthcare, health systems); OR
   - indirectly, via a recognised climate-health exposure pathway (CCHE): air quality; extreme weather events; food supply / food security; heat stress; social factors (displacement, migration, conflict); vector distribution and ecology; water quality and quantity (including harmful algal blooms).
   A recognised exposure pathway counts ON MENTION -- it need not be framed as affecting a specific population, need not be "water people use", and need not carry a named clinical outcome.

(b) MITIGATION -- the record concerns ANY action, intervention, technology, practice, policy, or management approach intended to reduce greenhouse-gas or other climate-forcing emissions, reduce or replace fossil-fuel use, or upscale greenhouse-gas removals. Per the guidance, ANY mitigation action counts (its emission reduction is treated as inherently health-relevant); a human-health or food-system connection is NOT required. Renewable energy, energy transition/storage, low-emission vehicles or vessels, cleaner industrial or chemical processes, carbon-footprint reduction, emission-regulation policy, reforestation, etc. all qualify. (Merely measuring a greenhouse gas, with no action, is not by itself mitigation -- but treat this generously.)

(c) ADAPTATION -- the record concerns ANY action, planning, assessment, model, dataset, or supporting research to prepare for, respond to, or reduce vulnerability/exposure to climate-related hazards: adaptation, preparedness, resilience, vulnerability reduction, risk reduction, climate-risk management, early warning, nature-based solutions, and disaster risk reduction. Disaster-risk-reduction and resilience framings qualify even when they are not exclusively climate-specific.

--------------------------------------------------
EXCLUDE only when:
--------------------------------------------------
- There is NO climate-related element at all (no climate factor, agent, event, fossil fuel, particulate matter, or climate-policy engagement); OR
- There is a climate-related element but NO health, mitigation, or adaptation element of any kind; OR
- The qualifying term is clearly incidental -- a stray word with no bearing on the record's content.
- The record is not a substantive publication in its own right (e.g. a bare citation or reference list with no research content of its own).

Do NOT exclude a record merely because:
- climate change, health, mitigation, or adaptation is not the main topic;
- the connection is brief, thematic, at the policy/framework level, or indirect;
- there is no human-health outcome (mitigation and many adaptation records have none);
- the study is environmental science, engineering, agriculture, energy, chemistry, hydrology, ecology, or policy;
- it is a review, bibliometric analysis, meta-analysis, modelling study, or dataset.

--------------------------------------------------
FINAL DECISION
--------------------------------------------------
Ask: (1) Is a climate-related element present (including a thematic or policy-level one)? (2) Is a health, mitigation, or adaptation element present? If both are plausibly yes, INCLUDE. When you remain genuinely uncertain, INCLUDE.

Return only the classification:

INCLUDE

or

EXCLUDE
